findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed there to be multiple food items out of cold holding temperatures in the bottom of the prep cooler closest to the dish area. Probed temperature of cut watermelon 46 degree F, Probed temperature of brisket 50 degrees F, ambient temperature on the internal thermometer of the cooler 50 degree F. These food items had recently been placed in this cooler from the walk in cooler. All items in this cooler were moved to the other cooler on the cook line. Ensure that all cold holding equipment keeps food items at or below 41 degrees Fahrenheit. Follow up has been scheduled for Tuesday, September 29, 2026 to ensure that cooler is keeping food at or below 41 degrees Fahrenheit.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed an accumulation of ice on the floor and ceiling of the walk in freezer. The PIC mentioned a work order will be placed to address this issue. Ensure that the walk in freezer is maintained and free of ice accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: There was a container of raw beef stored above cooked seafood in a prep cooler along the cookline. The items were rearranged to correct the violation. Ensure that raw animal proteins are never stored above any ready-to-eat (RTE) foods to protect against cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: All sanitizer solutions throughout the restaurants were testing less than 100ppm (quat). These included sanitizer from the main triple sink and all buckets stored along the cookline. The sanitizer bag connected to the sink dispenser was observed empty. The bag was replaced by the PIC and retested at 200ppm to correct the violation. Ensure that sanitizer solutions are testing at the manufacturer’s recommended concentrations to effectively sanitize food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector probed heavy cream in the beverage cooler of the facility. Heavy cream probed at 50F. It and another carton of half and half were discarded immediately by the PIC. Ensure that TCS foods are always kept at or below 41F.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the beverage cooler to not be holding food at 41F or below. See violation 22 for foods. Inspector originally observed the cooler holding food at ~50F. Inspector watched PIC discard food, and then had the cooler closed and left until the end of the inspection. At the end of the inspection, the cooler was holding ~49F. Ensure cooler is serviced so that it holds food at or below 41F.

Inspector will return 10/09/2025 to re-inspect cooler.

Ensure quat dispenser and sani-buckets are tested every day to maintain proper concentrations of sanitizer.

Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.citation_text:
750.240 - Bag of frozen shrimp was observed thawing under cold running water in the front area prep sink. Only the bottom of the bag was in contact with water. Product was placed in a container under running water so all surfaces were in contact with water during thawing process.

Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the  following methods: 1. Under refrigeration 41F/below, 2. Under  potable running water 70F/below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, or 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: 750-510d Observed a common towel being used to wipe wet and soiled hands. Discussed using common towels with staff. Cease using a common towel to wipe wet hands and counters. Use a disposable paper towel. To avoid re-contaminating their hands, food employees shall use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a hand-washing sink or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment: 750-530a Observed lamb stroganoff on the top shelf of the walk-in cooler. Stroganoff is a personal food item. Food was moved to the bottom shelf during the inspection. Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.comment: 750-820d Observed multiple students improperly sanitizing equipment in the third sink of the three compartment sink. Multiple students were observed washing, rinsing, and then dipping bowls, peelers, and other tools into the sanitizing sink for less than the required contact time. Discuss sanitizing practices with students. Make sure entire facility is aware of the sixty second contact time. Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).

Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - Boiled eggs observed in top of prep cooler had surface temperature of 64F. Eggs were observed out in prep area upon arrival of inspectors. Executive Chef stated the eggs were boiled, peeled, and sliced w/in the hour. Time and temperature were not being tracked for cooling eggs. Eggs were taken to blast chiller to help quickly drop the product to 41F.

Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41F. Mark time on cooling foods and monitor the temperature to ensure foods are reaching benchmark temperatures in designated time frame for proper cooling (135F to 70F w/in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs - total cooling time 6hrs).

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Sliced turkey in top of prep cooler had internal temperature of 54F. Turkey was observed sitting out in prep area while chefs were doing prep prior to placing product in prep cooler. Turkey was in the cooler for at least 15-20 minutes prior to temperature check. Executive Chef placed turkey in blast chiller to quickly drop temperature.

Cold potentially hazardous foods must be maintained at 41F/below. **Do not get foods out until they are ready to be prepped and/or transported to another area for use (i.e. from walkin cooler to prep cooler, etc.). Get out only what is needed for prep and immediately place items in coolers after prep is completed.**

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact

750.160 & 280 - Person observed having bare hand contact with tomatoes being sliced for use at the salad cooler. Student washed hands and put on gloves to finish prep.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).

750.1120 - Person working in dish area was observed wiping hands on cloth towel. Proper use of wiping cloths was discussed with intern and manager. 
Wash hands between handling dirty dishes and prior to handling clean dishes after items go through the dish machine. Always use paper towels only to dry/wipe hands.
Use only paper towels for wiping hands between tasks when working with soiled equipment.

Common towels are prohibited for use.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
750-830 The wall mounted quat dispenser is not properly dispensing sanitizing solution. Ecolab was present within the last few days to service the system. This wall-mounted unit is used to fill sani-buckets for food and non-food contact surfaces and the three compartment sink. During the inspection, it was discovered that the quat product container was empty. The product was replaced. Solution was tested at proper concentration. Sani-buckets previously filled with improper solution were refilled.

All chemical sanitizers must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text:
750.860 - Clean utensils were observed with food contact surfaces stored up out of containers. Utensils were flipped so handles were presented out of storage containers.

Cleaned and sanitized utensils and equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means. findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.comment:
Multiple frozen foods (chicken wings, meats, sausage, vegetable stock, soups, etc.) found in walk-in freezer that were vacuum-packaged on site.  Operator states most of these items are for classroom use only. Once the plan has been submitted and approved, vacuum packaging may be done at the facility.  This includes sous-vide items.

750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the ate or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.
